Sing loudly at the same time
98378.e: You hold your hand in front of your open mouth. That is considered polite.
98378.m: When you yawn, you put your hand in front of your mouth.

98379.q: Apart from tiredness, when else do we often yawn?
98379.e: Boredom also makes us yawn. Many people know this from long waits.

98380.q: What do people often do together with yawning when they wake up?
98380.e: After waking up, many people yawn and stretch their arms and legs. That wakes the muscles up.
98380.m: After waking up, you yawn and stretch.

98381.q: What is it called when someone gets up and walks around in their sleep?
98381.e: When sleepwalking, someone gets up in their sleep and walks around without really being awake.
98381.m: Someone who walks around in their sleep is sleepwalking.

98382.e: Sleepwalking happens much more often in children than in adults.

98383.q: Does a sleepwalker remember it in the morning?
98383.e: Sleepwalkers are not really awake. That is why they usually know nothing about it in the morning.
98383.m: Sleepwalkers usually do not remember it.

98384.q: What should you do with a sleepwalker?
a: Calmly lead them back to bed
98384.e: You gently lead a sleepwalker back to bed. You should not frighten them.
98384.m: You calmly lead a sleepwalker back to bed.

98385.q: What are the eyes often like during sleepwalking?
98385.e: Sleepwalkers often have their eyes open. Even so, they are asleep and staring into space.
98385.m: Sleepwalkers often have their eyes open.

98386.q: Does sleepwalking in children usually stop again?
98386.e: In most children, sleepwalking stops by itself by the teenage years.

98387.q: What protects a sleepwalker from accidents?
a: Stretching a rope across the room
98387.e: Safe stairs and windows prevent falls. Things lying around should be tidied away.
98387.m: Safe stairs and windows protect sleepwalkers.

98388.q: Is a sleepwalker awake while walking around?
98388.e: Sleepwalking happens in deep sleep, usually in the first half of the night. That is why the sleepwalker notices nothing.

98389.q: What can make sleepwalking happen more often?
98389.e: Lack of sleep can trigger sleepwalking. So getting enough sleep helps against it.

98390.q: Mia sleeps 10 hours every night. How many hours does she sleep in a week?
98390.e: A week has 7 nights. 7 times 10 hours makes 70 hours.

98391.q: How many hours of sleep do adults need each night?
98391.e: Adults are advised to get 7 to 9 hours of sleep a night.
98391.m: Adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep.

98392.e: Newborn babies sleep about 14 to 17 hours a day, spread over lots of little naps.

98393.q: Roughly how much of their life do people spend asleep?
98393.e: If you sleep 8 out of 24 hours, you sleep a third of the day. So you spend about a third of your life asleep.
98393.m: We spend about a third of our lives asleep.

98394.q: Which animal sleeps up to 20 hours a day?
98394.e: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves, which provide little energy. That is why they sleep and rest for up to 20 hours a day.
98394.m: The koala is a great sleeper.

98395.q: Tim gets up at 7 o'clock and wants to sleep for 10 hours. When does he need to go to bed?
98395.e: From 9 pm to 7 am is 10 hours. You work out 7 o'clock minus 10 hours.
98395.m: If you get up early, you need to go to bed early.

98396.q: Lea sleeps from 8 pm to 7 am. How many hours is that?
98396.e: From 8 pm to midnight is 4 hours, from midnight to 7 am is 7 hours. 4 plus 7 makes 11 hours.
98396.m: You add up the hours of sleep across midnight.

98397.q: How many hours of sleep do teenagers aged 13 to 18 need?
98397.e: Teenagers need about 8 to 10 hours of sleep, a bit more than adults.
98397.m: Teenagers need 8 to 10 hours of sleep.

98398.q: What are the clothes you put on to sleep called?
98398.e: Pyjamas are comfortable clothes for the night. You put them on before going to sleep.

98399.q: In which country do pyjamas have their origin?
98399.e: Pyjamas originally come from India and its neighbouring countries. The British brought them to Europe.

98400.q: Which two parts do pyjamas usually have?
98400.e: Pyjamas usually have a top and long or short trousers.
98400.m: Pyjamas have a top and trousers.

98401.q: What is a long shirt for sleeping in without trousers called?
98401.e: A nightdress is a long, loose shirt for the night. No trousers go with it.
98401.m: A nightdress is a long shirt for sleeping.

98402.q: Which fabric is popular for pyjamas because it is soft and soaks up sweat?
98402.e: Cotton is soft, feels pleasant on the skin and soaks up sweat well.
98402.m: Cotton pyjamas are soft and comfortable.

98403.q: Why do you put on pyjamas to sleep?
98403.e: Pyjamas are loose and soft. And you do not bring the dirt from the day into bed.

98405.q: What do you wear with your pyjamas in winter against cold feet?
98405.e: Warm socks keep your feet warm. With warm feet, you fall asleep more easily.
98405.m: Warm socks help against cold feet in bed.

98406.q: Which colour of light from screens disturbs sleep most?
98406.e: Screens give off a lot of blue light. It tells the body that it is still daytime and keeps you awake.
98406.m: Blue screen light keeps you awake.

98407.q: When is it best to put screens away before going to sleep?
98407.e: Experts advise putting screens away about an hour before going to sleep. That way the body can wind down.
98407.m: Put screens away about an hour before going to sleep.

98408.q: Where is the best place for your phone at night?
a: In bed next to your head
98408.e: In the bedroom, messages and light from the phone can disturb your sleep. That is why it is better left outside.
98408.m: Your phone sleeps better outside the bedroom.

98409.q: What is better than a screen before falling asleep?
98409.e: A book does not glow and does not get you excited. Reading calms you before sleep.
98409.m: Before sleeping, it is better to read a book.

98410.q: What often happens to your eyes after a lot of screen time?
98410.e: When you look at a screen, you blink less. That is why your eyes get tired and dry.
98410.m: A lot of screen time makes your eyes tired.

98411.q: What helps you keep track of your screen time?
98411.e: With a timer or alarm clock you know when your time is up.
98411.m: A timer helps you stick to your screen time.

98412.q: What is better for the body than hours in front of a screen?
98412.e: Moving in the fresh air strengthens muscles and bones. In the evening you are then pleasantly tired.
98412.m: Playing outside is good for the body.

98413.q: What does an exciting screen game in the evening do to the brain?
98413.e: Exciting games stimulate the brain. Afterwards it takes longer to fall asleep.
98413.m: Exciting games in the evening keep the brain awake.

98414.q: How many wheels does a normal bicycle have?
98414.e: A normal bicycle has a front wheel and a back wheel, so 2 wheels.

98415.q: What was still missing on the very first running machine?
98415.e: The first running machine was built in 1817. You pushed yourself along with your feet on the ground, because there were no pedals yet.
98415.m: The first running machine had no pedals yet.

98416.q: What was special about the penny-farthing, an old bicycle?
a: Three wheels of the same size
98416.e: On a penny-farthing the front wheel was very big and the back wheel small. The pedals were attached directly to the front wheel.
98416.m: The penny-farthing had a huge front wheel.

98417.q: What do you sit on when you ride a bike?
98417.e: The saddle is the seat of the bike. It should be high enough for your legs to be almost straight when you pedal.
98417.m: When cycling you sit on the saddle.

98418.q: What do you steer a bike with?
98418.e: With the handlebars you turn the front wheel left or right. That is how you choose your direction.

98419.q: Where at the back of a bike can you fix a bag?
98419.e: The pannier rack sits at the back above the rear wheel. You can fix bags or a basket to it.
98419.m: You carry bags on the pannier rack.

98420.q: Why does a moving bike not fall over as easily as one standing still?
98420.e: A moving bike is easy to keep balanced. Small steering movements stop it from tipping over.
98420.m: A moving bike stays balanced more easily.

98421.q: From what age may children in Switzerland ride a bike alone on a main road?
98421.e: In Switzerland children from the age of 6 may ride alone on main roads. Younger children need someone with them who is at least 16.
98421.m: You may ride alone on a main road from age 6.

98422.q: In Switzerland, must every bike have a bell?
98422.e: In Switzerland every bike must have a bell. You can use it to warn others.
98422.m: A bike bell is compulsory in Switzerland.

98423.q: Up to what age may children in Switzerland cycle on the pavement if there is no cycle path?
98423.e: Children may ride on the pavement until their 12th birthday if there is no cycle path or cycle lane. They must look out for pedestrians.
98423.m: Children up to 12 may cycle carefully on the pavement.

98424.q: A bike has 2 chainrings at the front and 10 sprockets at the back. How many gears does it have?
98424.e: Each of the 2 chainrings works with each of the 10 sprockets. 2 times 10 makes 20 gears.
98424.m: Count the gears as chainrings times sprockets.

98425.q: Where are the brake levers on most bikes?
98425.e: The brake levers are on the handlebars. So you can brake with your hands without letting go.
98425.m: The brake levers are on the handlebars.

98426.q: How do you brake with a coaster brake?
a: You put your feet on the ground
98426.e: With a coaster brake you push the pedals backwards. Then the rear wheel brakes.
98426.m: With a coaster brake you pedal backwards.

98427.q: What is produced at the brakes when you brake?
98427.e: When you brake, the brake pads rub. The friction makes the brakes warm.

98428.q: When is a bike's braking distance longer?
98428.e: On wet roads and with wet brakes, everything grips less well. That is why it takes longer to stop.
98428.m: In the wet a bike takes longer to stop.

98429.q: Which bike brake presses brake blocks against the edge of the wheel?
98429.e: The rim brake presses two brake blocks against the rim, the edge of the wheel.
98429.m: The rim brake brakes on the edge of the wheel.

98430.q: Which bike brake has a metal disc in the middle of the wheel?
98430.e: With a disc brake, a metal disc is fixed to the wheel hub. Brake pads grip this disc.
98430.m: The disc brake brakes on a metal disc.

98431.q: What is the safest way to brake?
a: With both brakes at the same time
Only with the front brake, very hard
With your feet on the ground
98431.e: Using both brakes together is the safest way to stop. Braking very hard with only the front brake can send you over the handlebars.
98431.m: The safest way to brake is with both brakes.

98432.q: Why does a bike have gears?
a: So that you can ride more easily or faster
So that the light comes on
So that the bell is louder
So that the saddle goes higher
98432.e: With gears you adjust how hard you pedal. Uphill you choose a low gear, on flat ground a high gear.
98432.m: Gears let you adjust the effort of pedalling.

98433.q: Which gear do you choose when the road goes steeply uphill?
98433.e: In a low gear the pedals are easy to turn. That way you can manage steep stretches too.
98433.m: Uphill you ride in a low gear.

98434.q: What are the small cogs on the rear wheel called?
98434.e: There are several cogs on the rear wheel, the sprockets. The chain runs over one of them.
98434.m: The cogs on the rear wheel are called sprockets.

98435.q: With which kind of gears can you see several cogs side by side on the rear wheel?
98435.e: With derailleur gears, a mechanism pushes the chain onto a different cog. With hub gears, the gears are hidden inside the hub.
98435.m: Derailleur gears move the chain from cog to cog.

98436.q: Where are the gears hidden with hub gears?
a: In the middle of the rear wheel
98436.e: With hub gears, the gears are built into the hub, that is, the middle of the rear wheel.
98436.m: With hub gears, the gears are hidden in the rear wheel.

98437.q: What do you have to do when changing gear with derailleur gears?
98437.e: The chain can only change when it is moving. So you have to keep pedalling while changing gear, but without much force.
98437.m: With derailleur gears you keep pedalling while changing.

98438.q: What is a high gear good for?
98438.e: In a high gear you go a long way with each turn of the pedals. That is good for riding fast on flat stretches.
98438.m: On flat ground you ride fast in a high gear.

98439.q: Where is the gear lever on most bikes?
98439.e: The gear levers are on the handlebars. So you can change gear while riding.
98439.m: The gear lever is on the handlebars.

98440.q: What does the chain do on a bike?
a: It takes the power to the rear wheel
It holds the saddle in place
98440.e: The chain connects the front cog with the rear wheel. That way the power of your legs drives the rear wheel.
98440.m: The chain takes the power of your legs to the rear wheel.

98441.q: What is a bike chain made of?
98441.e: A bike chain is made of many small steel links. They are joined together so they can move.
98441.m: A bike chain is made of many metal links.

98442.q: What does a bike chain need to run well?
98442.e: Chain oil lubricates the links. That way the chain runs quietly and rusts less.

98443.q: What happens to a chain that often gets wet and is never looked after?
98443.e: Steel rusts when it gets wet. Looking after it with oil protects the chain.

98444.q: What is a chain guard on a bike good for?
98444.e: The chain guard covers the chain. That way your trousers and fingers stay clean and do not get caught in the chain.
98444.m: The chain guard protects trousers and fingers.

98445.q: What does the bike chain run over at the front, by the pedals?
98445.e: At the front, on the crank, there is a large cog, the chainring. The chain fits into its teeth.
98445.m: At the front the chain runs over the chainring.

98446.q: What can happen if the chain is loose?
98446.e: A loose or badly adjusted chain can jump off the cog. Then you cannot pedal the bike forward any more.
98446.m: A loose chain can come off.

98447.q: What fits into the gaps in the chain?
98447.e: The teeth of the cogs fit exactly into the gaps in the chain. That way it does not slip.
98447.m: The teeth of the cogs fit into the chain.

98448.q: What do you use to push the pedals?
98448.e: Your feet rest on the pedals and push them round in a circle.
98448.m: You push the pedals with your feet.

98449.q: What movement do the pedals make when you ride?
a: They go round in a circle
98449.e: The pedals are attached to the cranks. When you pedal, they go round in a circle.
98449.m: The pedals go round in a circle.

98450.q: What colour are the reflectors on the pedals in Switzerland?
98450.e: Pedal reflectors are orange or yellow. They move as you pedal, so they stand out well in headlights.
98450.m: Pedal reflectors are orange or yellow.

98451.q: What are the arms the pedals are attached to called?
98451.e: The cranks connect the pedals to the chainring. They work like levers.
98451.m: The pedals are attached to the cranks.

98452.q: Why do people sometimes stand up on the pedals when going uphill?
a: To push with their body weight
98452.e: When you stand, your own body weight presses on the pedals. That way you can put in more force.
98452.m: Standing up, your body weight presses hard on the pedals.

98453.q: Which part of your foot is best for pushing the pedal?
98453.e: With the ball of your foot on the pedal you can pass on the most force.
98453.m: Pedal with the ball of your foot.

98454.q: What is special about clipless pedals?
a: The shoe clicks into the pedal
98454.e: With clipless pedals, a plate on the shoe clicks into the pedal. That way your foot does not slip off.
98454.m: With clipless pedals the shoe clicks in.

98455.q: How many pedals does a normal bike have?
98455.e: A bike has one pedal for the left foot and one for the right.

98456.q: What colour is the rear light on a bike?
98456.e: The light at the back of a bike is red. Cars have red rear lights too.
98456.m: A bike's rear light is red.

98457.q: When must you switch on your bike lights in Switzerland?
a: At night and when visibility is poor
98457.e: At night, in tunnels and when visibility is poor, bikes must have lights at the front and back.
98457.m: At night and in poor visibility a bike needs lights.

98458.q: Why do you need lights on your bike at dusk?
a: So that the bike gets warmer
98458.e: With lights, drivers and pedestrians see you much sooner. You can also see the way better yourself.

98459.q: Where in Switzerland must you ride with lights on even during the day?
98459.e: It is dark in a tunnel. That is why you need bike lights there even during the day.
98459.m: In a tunnel a bike always needs lights.

98460.q: Where does a bike light without a dynamo get its electricity from?
a: From a battery or rechargeable battery
From the air in the tyre
98460.e: Many bike lights have a battery or a rechargeable battery. You charge the rechargeable battery at a socket.
98460.m: Bike lights without a dynamo need a battery.

98461.q: What must you do if a bike light with a rechargeable battery stops working?
98461.e: A flat battery gives no more electricity. After charging, the light works again.
98461.m: A flat battery must be charged again.

98462.q: Which kind of light on bikes is bright and saves energy?
98462.e: LED lights are very bright and use little electricity. That is why almost all bike lights have LEDs today.
98462.m: LED lights are bright and save energy.

98463.q: What do you have to do with a bottle dynamo to make the light come on?
98463.e: A bottle dynamo only works when its little wheel is touching the tyre. So to switch it on, you flip it against the tyre.
98463.m: You flip a bottle dynamo against the tyre.

98464.q: When does a light with a simple dynamo shine?
a: When the bike is standing still
98464.e: The dynamo only makes electricity while the wheel is turning. When the bike stops, a simple dynamo light goes out.
98464.m: A dynamo only makes electricity when the wheel turns.

a: In the middle of the front wheel
98465.e: The hub dynamo is built into the hub of the front wheel, that is, the middle of the wheel.
98465.m: The hub dynamo sits in the middle of the front wheel.

98466.q: What does a bottle dynamo rub against?
98466.e: A small wheel on the bottle dynamo presses against the side of the tyre. When the tyre turns, the little wheel turns too.
98466.m: The bottle dynamo turns along with the tyre.

98467.q: What is inside a dynamo and helps to make electricity?
98467.e: Inside the dynamo, a magnet turns next to a coil of wire. This produces electricity.
98467.m: In a dynamo a turning magnet makes electricity.

98468.q: What do you often notice when pedalling with the dynamo switched on?
98468.e: To make electricity, the dynamo needs some force. This force comes from your legs.
98468.m: The dynamo's electricity takes a bit of leg power.

98469.q: What does the standlight on a bike with a dynamo do?
a: It keeps shining when you stop
It only shines when it rains
It goes off when you brake
98469.e: A standlight stores a little electricity. So the lamp keeps shining for a while when you wait at the traffic lights.
98469.m: A standlight keeps shining when you stop.

98470.q: Does a light with a dynamo need a battery?
a: Yes, but only at the back
98470.e: The dynamo makes the electricity itself as long as you are riding. That is why you do not need a battery.
98470.m: A dynamo light needs no battery.

98471.q: Where are the stabilisers on a child's bike?
a: On the left and right of the rear wheel
At the front on the handlebars
On top of the front wheel
98471.e: The two small stabiliser wheels are fixed on the left and right of the rear wheel.
98471.m: Stabilisers are next to the rear wheel.

a: To stop the bike from tipping over
98472.e: Stabilisers keep the bike upright. That way it does not tip to the side even when standing still.
98472.m: Stabilisers stop the bike tipping over.

98473.q: What do you hardly learn with stabilisers?
98473.e: With stabilisers you do not have to balance. That is why you hardly learn balance with them.
98473.m: With stabilisers you hardly learn to balance.

98474.q: What do many children use today instead of stabilisers to learn balance?
98474.e: On a balance bike you push off with your feet and balance at the same time. That is how you learn balance.
98474.m: On a balance bike you learn to balance.

98475.q: What can happen in a fast bend with stabilisers?
98475.e: With stabilisers you cannot lean into the bend. At high speed the bike therefore easily tips outwards.
98475.m: Bikes with stabilisers can tip over in fast bends.

98476.q: How many stabilisers does a child's bike usually have?
98476.e: A child's bike usually has two stabilisers, one on each side.
98476.m: A child's bike usually has two stabilisers.

98477.q: When do you take the stabilisers off?
98477.e: Once the child can keep their balance alone, they no longer need stabilisers.
98477.m: If you can balance, you no longer need stabilisers.

98478.q: A bike has two wheels and two stabilisers. How many wheels is that altogether?
98478.e: The front wheel and back wheel are 2 wheels. Then there are 2 stabilisers. 2 plus 2 makes 4.
98478.m: Two wheels and two stabilisers make four wheels.

98479.q: What do you pump into a bike tyre?
98479.e: Inside the tyre is an inner tube full of air. The air makes the tyre firm and springy.
98479.m: You pump air into a bike tyre.

98480.q: What do you use to pump up a bike tyre?
98480.e: With a bike pump you push air through the valve into the inner tube.
98480.m: A bike pump puts air into the tyre.

98481.q: Through which part does the air get into the inner tube?
98481.e: The valve lets air in but not back out. That way the tyre stays firm.
98481.m: Air gets into the inner tube through the valve.

98482.q: In which unit is tyre pressure often measured?
98482.e: The pressure in a tyre is often given in bar. The right number is usually printed on the tyre.
98482.m: Tyre pressure is measured in bar.

98483.q: What is it like riding a bike with too little air in the tyres?
98483.e: A soft tyre squashes a lot. It rolls less well, and you have to pedal harder.
98483.m: With too little air, a bike is hard work to ride.

98484.q: What happens if an inner tube has a hole?
98484.e: Air streams out through a hole. The tyre goes flat and you have a ‘puncture’.
98484.m: If there is a hole, the air escapes from the tyre.

98485.q: Who built an air-filled tyre for his son's tricycle in 1887 and made it well known?
98485.e: John Boyd Dunlop built an air-filled tyre for his son's tricycle in 1887 and patented it in 1888. It made the ride much smoother.
98485.m: Dunlop made the air-filled tyre well known.

98486.q: How do you find a small hole in an inner tube?
a: You put it in the sun
98486.e: In water, air bubbles rise where the hole is. That way you can see it exactly.
98486.m: In water, bubbles give the hole away.

98487.q: How should a bike helmet sit?
a: Straight and firm on your head
Loose at the back of your neck
98487.e: A helmet only protects you if it sits straight on your head and covers your forehead. It must not wobble.
98487.m: A helmet sits straight and firm on your head.

98488.q: What holds a bike helmet in place under your chin?
98488.e: The chin strap is fastened under your chin. That way the helmet stays on your head if you fall.
98488.m: The chin strap holds the helmet in place.

98489.q: What should you do with your helmet after a bad fall?
a: Wash it and keep wearing it
98489.e: In a fall, the foam inside the helmet can be damaged, even if you cannot see it. That is why you need a new helmet afterwards.
98489.m: After a bad fall you need a new helmet.

98490.q: Is a bike helmet compulsory in Switzerland for normal bikes?
98490.e: For normal bikes there is no helmet requirement in Switzerland (as of 2025). But experts strongly recommend wearing one.
98490.m: A bike helmet is not compulsory, but strongly recommended.

98491.q: What is inside a bike helmet that absorbs the impact?
98491.e: There is hard foam inside the helmet. It is squashed in an impact and so protects your head.
98491.m: The foam in a helmet absorbs the impact.

98492.q: Why does a bike helmet have holes?
a: So that air cools your head
So that it breaks more easily
So that you can hear better
98492.e: Air flows through the vents. That way you sweat less under the helmet.
98492.m: The holes in a helmet let air through.

98493.q: Which helmet colour is especially easy to see in traffic?
98493.e: Light, bright colours stand out well in traffic. Dark helmets are harder to see.
98493.m: A bright helmet is easy to see.

98494.q: What is another name for a bike reflector?
98494.e: Reflectors are also called cat's eyes. Cats' eyes also light up in the dark when light shines into them.
98494.m: A reflector is also called a cat's eye.

98495.q: Does a reflector light up by itself?
98495.e: A reflector has no lamp. It sends back the light that falls on it, for example from a car.
98495.m: A reflector sends back light from elsewhere.

98496.q: What colour is the reflector at the back of a bike?
98496.e: There must be a red reflector at the back of a bike. It matches the colour of the rear light.
98496.m: The reflector at the back of a bike is red.

98497.q: What colour is the reflector at the front of a bike?
98497.e: There must be a white reflector at the front of a bike. That way people can tell which is the front.
98497.m: The reflector at the front of a bike is white.

98498.q: In which direction does a reflector send the light?
98498.e: A reflector sends the light back to where it came from. That way the driver behind the headlights can see it well.
98498.m: A reflector sends light back towards the lamp.

98499.q: When can you see a reflector best?
a: In total darkness with no light
98499.e: A reflector needs light from outside. Without light it stays dark.
98499.m: A reflector needs light to shine.

98500.q: What do you wear in the dark so that you are seen better on foot or on a bike?
98500.e: Reflectors on clothes send back the light from cars. That way you are seen much sooner.
98500.m: Reflectors on your clothes make you visible.

98501.q: Where does the cat's eye on a bike get its name from?
a: It shines in the light like a cat's eyes
It is as small as a cat's eye
It is green like a cat's eye
It is round like a cat's eye
98501.e: Cats have a layer behind the retina that reflects light. That is why their eyes shine in headlights, just like a reflector.
98501.m: Cats' eyes shine in the light like reflectors.

98502.q: What do you call a road that goes over a high mountain, like the Gotthard?
98502.e: A pass is a road over a mountain crossing. On a bike it goes steeply uphill for a long way.

98503.q: What happens going downhill if you do not pedal?
98503.e: Downhill, gravity pulls the bike down. It rolls faster and faster, so you have to brake.
98503.m: Downhill a bike speeds up by itself.

98504.q: What can you do if a hill is too steep to ride up?
a: Get off and push the bike
Let the air out of the tyres
98504.e: If it is too steep, you get off and push. That is completely normal and safe.
98504.m: If it is too steep, push the bike.

98505.q: What helps on an e-bike going uphill?
98505.e: On an e-bike, an electric motor helps you pedal. That way you get up the hill more easily.
98505.m: On an e-bike a motor helps you pedal.

98506.q: What is especially important when riding a bike downhill?
98506.e: Downhill you go fast. You must brake early and with both brakes so that you do not go too fast.

98507.q: What is the easiest way to pedal uphill?
98507.e: Steady, calm pedalling saves energy. If you pedal jerkily, you get tired more quickly.

98508.q: Who finds it easier to ride a bike up a hill?
98508.e: The less weight you have to take uphill, the less effort you need.
98508.m: Less weight makes riding uphill easier.

98509.q: Where in Switzerland do you often have to cycle uphill?
a: Along the shore of Lake Constance
98509.e: The Alps have many steep roads and passes. There you often go uphill for a long way.
98509.m: In the Alps you often cycle uphill.

99009.q: Which flower is often called the “queen of flowers”?
99009.e: The rose has been one of the most popular flowers for a very long time. That is why it is often called the queen of flowers.
99009.m: The rose is known as the queen of flowers.

99010.q: When are garden roses usually cut back hard?
99010.e: In spring, when no more hard frost is coming, old and dead shoots are cut off. Afterwards strong new shoots with flowers grow.
99010.m: Roses are cut back in spring.

99011.q: What colour is the rose given as a sign of love?
99011.e: A red rose has long been a sign of love. People give it on Valentine's Day, for example.
99011.m: The red rose is a sign of love.

99012.q: What are many roses known for when you sniff them?
99012.e: Many roses smell sweet and delicate. Their petals are even used to make scented oil.

99013.q: Which fruit belongs to the same plant family as the rose?
99013.e: The rose and the apple both belong to the rose family. Cherries and strawberries are in it too.
99013.m: The apple is related to the rose.

99014.q: How many petals does a simple wild rose usually have?
99014.e: Wild roses such as the dog rose usually have five petals. Garden roses often have many more.
99014.m: A wild rose usually has five petals.

99015.q: What do you cut off roses in summer so that new flowers come?
99015.e: If you cut off faded flowers, the rose puts its strength into new flowers. That way it flowers for longer.
99015.m: Faded rose flowers are cut off.

99016.q: What does a rose in the garden especially need to flower well?
99016.e: Roses love a sunny spot. In the shade they flower much less.

99017.q: What is a rose that grows up walls and arches called?
99017.e: Climbing roses have long shoots. They are tied to trellises, arches or house walls.
99017.m: A climbing rose grows up walls.

99018.q: What do many people call the pelargonium in the window box?
99018.e: The popular balcony flower is really called a pelargonium. But in everyday life most people say geranium.
99018.m: The balcony geranium is really a pelargonium.

99019.q: What are the wild relatives of the geranium that also grow in Swiss meadows called?
99019.e: Geraniums and cranesbills belong to the same plant family. Their fruits look like a long bird's beak.
99019.m: The cranesbill is a wild relative of the geranium.

99020.q: Which continent do most geraniums come from?
99020.e: Most balcony geraniums originally come from southern Africa. It is warm and sunny there.

99021.q: What can geraniums not cope with at all?
99021.e: Geraniums die in frost. That is why they are brought indoors in autumn.
99021.m: Geraniums must be protected from frost.

99022.q: What do geraniums in pots not like at all?
99022.e: Geraniums need regular watering. But if water is left standing in the pot, their roots rot.
99022.m: Geraniums don't like standing water in the pot.

99023.q: What colour are geraniums in Switzerland very often?
99023.e: There are geraniums in red, pink, white and purple. The best known are the red geraniums.
99023.m: Many geraniums have bright red flowers.

99024.q: What happens with some geraniums when you rub their leaves?
99024.e: With scented geraniums, the leaves smell of lemon or rose, for example, when rubbed. That is why they are called that.
99024.m: Scented geraniums smell when you rub their leaves.

99025.q: Which spot do geraniums like best?
99025.e: Geraniums come from a warm, sunny country. They flower most beautifully in the sun.

99026.q: In which season do sunflowers bloom?
99026.e: Sunflowers bloom in summer, when it is warm and sunny. In autumn the seeds then ripen.

99027.q: What does the stem of a sunflower feel like?
99027.e: The stem and leaves of the sunflower are covered in small, stiff hairs. That is why they feel rough.
99027.m: The sunflower's stem is rough and hairy.

99028.q: In what pattern do the seeds sit in a sunflower?
99028.e: The seeds are arranged in many spirals running to the left and to the right. That way a great many seeds fit on the flower head.
99028.m: The sunflower's seeds sit in spirals.

99029.q: Which insects like to collect nectar from sunflowers?
99029.e: The sunflower's many small flowers offer nectar and pollen. That is why bees and bumblebees like to visit them.

99030.q: Which continent does the sunflower come from?
99030.e: The sunflower first grew in North America. Sailors brought it to Europe a long time ago.
99030.m: The sunflower comes from North America.

99031.q: Which animals like eating sunflower seeds at the bird table in winter?
99031.e: Tits and other birds like pecking at sunflower seeds. The seeds give them a lot of energy.

99032.q: How tall can a sunflower in the garden grow?
a: Only as tall as a shoe
99032.e: Many sunflowers grow two to three metres tall. That makes them taller than adults.
99032.m: Sunflowers can grow taller than a person.

99033.q: What does a sunflower need to grow well?
99033.e: As its name says, the sunflower loves the sun. In a bright, warm spot it grows big and strong.

99034.q: What is the big brown centre of the sunflower really?
99034.e: The centre is made of a great many tiny flowers. Each little flower later becomes a seed.
99034.m: The centre of the sunflower is made of many small flowers.

99035.q: Which country does the dahlia come from?
99035.e: Dahlias grow wild in Mexico. There the dahlia is even the national flower.

99036.q: What do dahlias grow from again each year?
99036.e: Dahlias form thick tubers in the ground. New shoots grow from them in spring.

99037.q: How big can the flowers of some dahlias get?
99037.e: There are very large dahlia varieties. Their flowers can get as wide as a plate.
99037.m: Some dahlias have flowers as big as a plate.

99039.e: Dahlias bloom from summer until the first frost. That way they bring colour to the garden in autumn too.
99039.m: Dahlias bloom from summer into autumn.

99040.q: Which flower colour do dahlias not come in?
99040.e: Dahlias come in almost every colour. But there is no truly blue dahlia.
99040.m: There are no truly blue dahlias.

99041.q: What do pompon dahlias look like?
99041.e: Pompon dahlias have lots of rolled-up petals. That is why their flowers are round like little balls.
99041.m: Pompon dahlias are round like balls.

99042.q: Which animals like to nibble young dahlias in spring?
99042.e: Slugs and snails love the tender young shoots of dahlias. That is why gardeners protect the plants well.
99042.m: Slugs and snails like eating young dahlias.

99044.q: What colours are marigold flowers usually?
99044.e: Marigolds glow a strong yellow and orange. Some also have reddish brown spots.
99044.m: Marigolds have yellow and orange flowers.

99045.q: What do the leaves of marigolds smell like?
99045.e: Marigolds have a strong, spicy smell. Some people like it, others don't.

99046.q: Why do gardeners like to plant marigolds between vegetables?
a: To make the vegetables grow faster
99046.e: The roots of marigolds drive away tiny worms in the soil. This keeps the vegetables healthier.
99046.m: Marigolds protect vegetables from pests in the soil.

99047.q: Which country do many marigolds come from?
99047.e: Marigolds originally come from Mexico and Central America. There they are used to decorate big festivals.

99048.q: How long does a marigold in the garden usually live?
99048.e: Most marigolds are annuals. They are sown again every spring.
99048.m: Marigolds are sown again every year.

99049.q: Which creatures especially like eating marigolds?
99049.e: Slugs and snails love marigolds. That is why marigolds can lure them away from other plants.
99049.m: Slugs and snails love eating marigolds.

99050.q: Until when do marigolds bloom in the garden?
99050.e: Marigolds bloom all summer. Only the first frost in autumn ends their flowering.
99050.m: Marigolds bloom until the first frost.

99051.q: When are pansies often planted on the balcony?
99051.e: Pansies cope well with cold. That is why they bloom in early spring, when other flowers are still asleep.

99052.q: What do the markings on many pansy flowers look like?
99052.e: The dark patches in the middle look like a little face. That is why children especially like this flower.
99052.m: Pansies often have a little face.

99053.q: Roughly how tall do pansies grow?
99053.e: Pansies stay small and grow only about 10 to 20 centimetres tall. That is why they fit well in bowls and boxes.

99054.q: What can you do with pansy flowers in the kitchen?
99054.e: Pansy flowers are edible. You can put them on a salad or a cake, for example.

99055.q: How many petals does a pansy have?
99055.e: A pansy has five petals. The bottom petal is the biggest.

99056.q: Which group of plants does the pansy belong to?
99056.e: The pansy is a kind of violet. Its scientific name begins with Viola, the name of the violets.
99056.m: The pansy belongs to the violets.

99057.e: There are pansies in yellow, blue, purple, white, orange and many mixtures. Often there are several colours on one flower.

99058.q: Where does the wild pansy grow?
99058.e: The wild pansy grows in meadows and fields. Its flowers are smaller than those of the garden kind.
99058.m: The wild pansy grows in meadows.

99059.q: What do hydrangea flowers often look like?
99059.e: Many hydrangeas have big, round flower heads. They are made of many small flowers.
99059.m: Hydrangeas often have round balls of flowers.

99060.q: What does a hydrangea need especially a lot of?
99060.e: Hydrangeas drink a lot. Their scientific name even means something like water vessel.
99060.m: Hydrangeas need a lot of water.

99061.q: What decides whether some hydrangeas flower blue or pink?
99061.e: In acidic soil with aluminium, some hydrangeas flower blue. In chalky soil they turn pink.
99061.m: The soil decides whether some hydrangeas turn blue or pink.

99062.q: Which spot do hydrangeas like best?
99062.e: In blazing sun hydrangeas quickly go limp. They like partial shade best.

99063.q: Which country does the garden hydrangea come from?
99063.e: The popular garden hydrangea comes from Japan. From there it came to Europe.
99063.m: The garden hydrangea comes from Japan.

99064.q: What often happens to hydrangea flowers in autumn?
99064.e: The flower balls dry on the bush and change colour. You can cut them for lovely dried bouquets.
99064.m: Dried hydrangea flowers are good for dried bouquets.

99065.q: Is a hydrangea a tree, a shrub or a grass?
99065.e: Hydrangeas grow as shrubs with several woody shoots. They usually grow about one to two metres tall.

99066.q: What do drooping, limp leaves on a hydrangea usually show?
99066.e: When the soil is too dry, hydrangeas let their leaves and flowers droop. After watering they often recover quickly.

99067.e: Hydrangeas bloom from early summer to late summer. Many flowers last a very long time.

99068.q: What does a lily grow from?
99068.e: Lilies form a bulb made of scales in the ground. A new stem grows from it every year.

99069.q: For which pet are lilies very poisonous?
99069.e: Even a little pollen or a few lily leaves can make cats seriously ill. Cat owners should not have lilies in the home.
99069.m: Lilies are very poisonous for cats.

99070.q: What do many lilies in a bunch of flowers smell like?
99070.e: Many lilies have a very strong, sweet scent. Some people even find it too strong in a room.
99070.m: Many lilies smell strong and sweet.

99071.e: The lily beetle is a bright red beetle. It and its larvae eat holes in lily leaves.
99071.m: The lily beetle is a red beetle that eats lily leaves.

99072.q: How many petals does a lily flower have?
99072.e: A lily has six petals. They often form a trumpet or a star.

99073.q: What colour is the Madonna lily?
99073.e: The Madonna lily has big white flowers. It is a very old garden plant.

99074.q: What can lily pollen do to clothes?
99074.e: Lily pollen is orange brown and stains strongly. That is why it is often picked off cut flowers.

99075.q: Which orange lily grows in sunny meadows in the Alps?
99075.e: The fire lily has bright orange flowers. In the Alps it likes to grow on sunny slopes.
99075.m: The fire lily glows orange in the Alps.

99076.q: Around which festival does the peony often bloom?
99076.e: The peony blooms in May and June. That is roughly the time of Whitsun, which is where its German name, Pfingstrose (Whitsun rose), comes from.

99077.q: In German the peony is called a “Whitsun rose”. Is it a real rose?
99077.e: The peony looks similar but belongs to a plant family of its own. It also has no thorns.
99077.m: The peony is not a real rose.

99078.q: Which small creatures often crawl on peony buds?
99078.e: The buds give off a sweet juice. The ants like it, and they do not harm the plant.

99079.q: What do peony flowers look like?
99079.e: Peonies have big, lush flowers. Many are double and round like a ball.

99080.q: How long can a peony grow in the same spot?
99080.e: A peony can live to a great age. In the same spot it often flowers for decades.
99080.m: Peonies can live for a very long time.

99081.q: What does a peony not like at all?
99081.e: Peonies do not like being moved. After transplanting they often do not flower for several years.
99081.m: It is better not to move peonies.

99082.e: Peonies flower in many shades from white through pink to dark red. There are also yellow varieties.
99082.m: Peonies often flower pink, red or white.

99083.q: What happens to the stems of a garden peony in autumn?
99083.e: In most garden peonies the stems wilt in autumn. In spring the plant grows again from the root.
99083.m: The peony grows again from the root every spring.

99084.q: Which small creatures often sit in crowds on nasturtiums?
99084.e: Black aphids love nasturtiums. That is why they are sometimes planted to lure aphids away from other plants.

99085.e: Nasturtium tastes slightly hot, similar to cress or pepper. This comes from a substance in the plant.

99086.e: The leaves are round and the stalk is attached in the middle. They look like little plates or umbrellas.
99086.m: Nasturtium has round leaves like little plates.

99087.q: What happens to drops of water on a nasturtium leaf?
a: They vanish into the leaf at once
99087.e: The leaves are water-repellent. The drops roll off like pearls and take dirt with them.

99088.q: What colours are nasturtium flowers often?
99088.e: The flowers glow in warm colours such as orange, yellow and red. They attract many insects.
99088.m: Nasturtiums flower orange, yellow or red.

99089.q: Which continent does the nasturtium come from?
99089.e: The nasturtium originally comes from the Andes in South America. Today it grows in many gardens.
99089.m: The nasturtium comes from South America.

99091.q: How does nasturtium often grow in the garden?
99091.e: Nasturtium forms long shoots. It creeps over the ground or climbs up fences.

99092.q: Where can you plant nasturtiums well if you have no garden?
99092.e: Nasturtium needs light and grows well in pots and boxes. The shoots then hang down nicely.
99092.m: Nasturtium grows well in a window box.

99093.q: What does the centre of a coneflower look like?
99093.e: The centre of the flower bulges upwards. That is why it reminds people of a little hat; in German the plant is called “sun hat”.
99093.m: The coneflower has a domed centre like a hat.

99094.q: What colour are the flowers of the purple coneflower?
99094.e: The purple coneflower flowers pink to purplish red. Its centre is orange brown.
99094.m: The purple coneflower flowers pink to purple.

99095.q: What colour is the yellow coneflower?
99095.e: In the yellow coneflower the petals are golden yellow. The centre is almost black.
99095.m: The yellow coneflower has a dark centre.

99096.q: Which continent does the coneflower come from?
99096.e: The coneflower grows wild in meadows in North America. Today it grows in many Swiss gardens.
99096.m: The coneflower comes from North America.

99097.q: Which creatures especially like visiting the coneflower?
99097.e: The coneflower has lots of nectar and pollen. That is why bees, bumblebees and butterflies like flying to it.
99097.m: Bees and butterflies love the coneflower.

99098.q: What is the purple coneflower also used for?
99098.e: Drops and tea are made from the purple coneflower, also called echinacea. They are used for colds, for example.
99098.m: The purple coneflower is a medicinal plant.

99099.q: Does the coneflower come back every year?
99099.e: The coneflower is a perennial. In winter it rests in the ground and sprouts again in spring.
99099.m: The coneflower comes back every year.

99100.q: Which spot does the coneflower like best?
99100.e: The coneflower loves the sun. In a bright spot it flowers abundantly.

99101.q: What colour are forget-me-not flowers usually?
99101.e: Forget-me-nots have small sky-blue flowers. They grow in little clusters.
99101.m: The forget-me-not usually flowers light blue.

99102.q: What colour is the small centre of a forget-me-not flower?
99102.e: In the middle of each blue flower there is a small yellow ring. It shows insects the way to the nectar.
99102.m: The forget-me-not has a yellow centre.

99103.e: The flowers are only a few millimetres across. But there are a great many at once.
99103.m: The forget-me-not has very small flowers.

99104.q: When does the forget-me-not bloom in the garden?
99104.e: The forget-me-not blooms in spring, often together with tulips. After that it fades.

99105.q: How many petals does a forget-me-not flower have?
99105.e: Each small flower has five petals. They are arranged around the yellow centre.

99106.q: What colour are forget-me-not buds often before they turn blue?
99106.e: The buds are often pink. When they open, the flowers turn blue.

99107.q: Where does the water forget-me-not grow?
99107.e: The water forget-me-not loves wet ground. You find it by streams, ponds and in marshes.
99107.m: The water forget-me-not grows by water.

99108.e: The name says: don't forget me. That is why the flower is given as a sign of remembrance.
99108.m: The forget-me-not is a sign of remembrance.

99195.q: Which finger do people especially often forget when washing their hands?
99195.e: The thumb sticks out a little and is often missed when rubbing. You should hold it with your other hand and wash it separately.
99195.m: When washing your hands, remember your thumbs.

99196.q: When must you always wash your hands?
99196.e: Before eating, you wash germs away so they do not get into your mouth with the food.
99196.m: You always wash your hands before eating.

99197.q: Why do you wash your hands after stroking a pet?
a: There can be germs on the fur
So the animal does not get cold
99197.e: Animals have germs in their fur and around their mouth that can make people ill. Washing your hands removes them.
99197.m: After stroking animals, you wash your hands.

99198.q: What do you do first when washing your hands?
99198.e: First you wet your hands, then you soap them. After that you rinse and dry them.
99198.m: When washing your hands, you wet them first.

99199.q: Why do you wash your hands after playing outside?
a: To make your hands smell nice
99199.e: Outside, your hands come into contact with soil and lots of germs. You wash them off with water and soap.
99199.m: Washing your hands removes dirt and germs.

99200.q: What do you do after washing your hands?
a: Rub your hands on your trousers
Put your hands in the soil
99200.e: Germs stick more easily to wet hands. That is why you dry them well with a clean towel after washing.
99200.m: After washing, you dry your hands well.

99201.q: Which doctor realised as early as about 1847 that hand washing protects patients?
99201.e: Ignaz Semmelweis had the doctors in his hospital clean their hands thoroughly. After that, far fewer patients became ill.
99201.m: Ignaz Semmelweis showed that clean hands save lives.

99202.q: What helps children wash their hands for long enough?
99202.e: Singing a short song like “Happy Birthday” twice takes about 20 seconds. That way you know when you are done.
99202.m: A song helps you wash your hands for long enough.

99203.q: What cleans your hands when you are out and there is no water?
99203.e: Hand sanitiser kills many germs. But if dirt is visible, washing with water and soap is better.

99204.q: What does soap do to dirt and grease?
99204.e: Soap loosens grease and dirt from the skin. Then you can rinse everything away with water.

99205.q: What has soap been made from for a long time?
99205.e: If you boil fat or oil with lye, soap is formed. People have made soap this way for thousands of years.
99205.m: Soap is made from fat and lye.

99206.q: What do you get when you rub soap with water?
99206.e: Soap and water together make lots of tiny bubbles. This foam helps with cleaning.

99207.q: What is the name of a simple, hard soap without perfume that people also used to wash clothes with in the past?
99207.e: Plain household soap is a simple, hard soap without perfume. In the past, people used it to wash their hands, bodies and clothes.
99207.m: Plain household soap is a simple, hard soap.

99208.q: What do you call soap that comes in a bottle with a pump?
99208.e: Liquid soap is runny and comes out of a dispenser. You just press the pump.
99208.m: Liquid soap comes from a pump dispenser.

99209.q: What happens to a bar of soap if you use it often?
99209.e: Every time you wash, a little soap dissolves in the water. That is why the bar gets smaller and smaller over time.
99209.m: Soap gets smaller as you use it.

99210.q: Where should a bar of soap be put after you use it?
a: In a soap dish to dry
99210.e: In a soap dish, the soap can drip and dry. If it lies in water, it becomes soft and slimy.
99210.m: Soap should be able to dry after washing.

99211.e: A full bathtub needs a lot of water. A short shower usually needs much less.

99212.q: Why do people shower after sport?
99212.e: You sweat when you do sport. Showering washes the sweat off, otherwise your skin soon starts to smell.
99212.m: After sport, you wash off the sweat in the shower.

99213.q: What can you turn off while you soap yourself in the shower?
99213.e: You do not need water while you are soaping yourself. If you turn it off for a moment, you save a lot of water.
99213.m: You can turn the water off while soaping yourself.

99214.q: Why do many showers have a rubber mat?
99214.e: Wet tiles are very slippery. A mat with little bumps helps you stand safely.
99214.m: A shower mat stops you from slipping.

99215.q: What must you do at an indoor swimming pool before you swim?
99215.e: You shower before swimming so that sweat and dirt do not get into the pool water. That keeps the water cleaner.

99216.q: What do you wash your body with in the shower?
99216.e: Shower gel is a liquid soap for the skin. Washing-up liquid is meant for dishes.
99216.m: You wash your body with shower gel or soap.

99217.q: How warm should shower water be?
99217.e: Water that is too hot can scald your skin and dries it out. Pleasantly warm water is best.
99217.m: Shower water should be pleasantly warm.

99218.q: Why do you shower after swimming at an indoor pool?
a: To wash off the chlorinated water
99218.e: Indoor pool water contains chlorine, which can dry out your skin. A shower afterwards rinses it off.
99218.m: After swimming, you rinse off the chlorine.

99219.q: What is the part of the shower that the water comes out of called?
99219.e: A shower head has lots of tiny holes. The water sprays out of them.
99219.m: The water comes out of the shower head.

99220.q: What do you check before you get into the bath?
99220.e: If the water is too hot, you can scald yourself. That is why you first check how warm it is.
99220.m: Before a bath, you check the water temperature.

99221.q: What is a good way to check how warm the bath water is?
99221.e: You put your hand or elbow into the water for a moment. That way you can feel whether it is too hot.
99221.m: You check bath water with your hand.

99222.q: Why must small children never be left alone in the bath?
99222.e: Small children can drown even in a little water. That is why an adult always stays with them.

99223.q: Why should bath toys be left to dry well after a bath?
99223.e: Water often stays inside hollow bath toys. Mould can grow there.
99223.m: Bath toys must dry after a bath.

99224.q: What do you dry yourself with after a bath?
99224.e: A big bath towel soaks up water well. That way you do not get cold after your bath.
99224.m: After a bath, you dry yourself with a bath towel.

a: Something you add to the bath to make foam
99225.e: You pour bubble bath into the running water. Then lots of mountains of foam form in the tub.
99225.m: Bubble bath makes foam in the bathtub.

99226.q: What do you do with the bath water after your bath?
99226.e: When you pull out the plug, the water drains away. Then you quickly rinse the tub.
99226.m: After a bath, you pull out the plug.

99227.q: Why do you also dry well between your toes after a bath?
a: So you do not get athlete's foot
99227.e: Athlete's foot is a fungus that likes damp, warm places. Well-dried toes help protect against it.
99227.m: Dry toes protect against athlete's foot.

99228.q: What is the best way to blow your nose?
a: On the back of your hand
99228.e: You hold one nostril closed and blow gently through the other. That way you do not push mucus into your ears.
99228.m: Blow gently, one nostril at a time.

99229.q: What do you do after blowing your nose?
99229.e: When you blow your nose, germs get onto your hands. Washing your hands stops you passing them on.
99229.m: After blowing your nose, you wash your hands.

99230.q: How often do you use a paper tissue?
99230.e: A paper tissue is meant to be used once. Next time you take a fresh one.
99230.m: You use a paper tissue only once.

99231.q: What are disposable tissues made of?
99231.e: Disposable tissues are made of soft, absorbent paper. That is why they are also called paper tissues.
99231.m: Disposable tissues are made of paper.

99233.q: When do you need especially many tissues?
99233.e: When you have a cold, your nose often runs. Then you blow it often with a fresh tissue.
99233.m: With a cold, you need lots of tissues.

99234.q: Why should you not touch other people's used tissues?
99234.e: Mucus can contain viruses and bacteria. You could catch something that way.
99234.m: Used tissues can pass on germs.

99235.q: How can you always have fresh tissues with you when you are out?
a: In a packet in your bag
Loose at the bottom of your rucksack
99235.e: A small packet keeps the tissues clean and dry. You can take it anywhere.
99235.m: Fresh tissues stay clean in their packet.

99236.q: What do some people wear to protect others when they cough?
99236.e: A face mask over the mouth and nose holds back many droplets. That way others are less likely to catch something.
99236.m: A face mask holds back droplets.

99237.q: Why should you not sneeze into your hands?
99237.e: You touch door handles and other people with your hands. That is how the germs get to others.
99237.m: Germs on your hands are quickly passed on.

99238.q: What flies out of your mouth and nose when you sneeze?
99238.e: When you sneeze, lots of tiny droplets spray out. They can contain germs.
99238.m: When you sneeze, tiny droplets fly through the air.

99239.q: What should you do when you need to cough?
a: Turn away and cough into the crook of your elbow
99239.e: You turn away from other people and cough into the crook of your elbow. That way fewer droplets reach others.
99239.m: When you cough, you turn away.

99240.q: Which illness often spreads through sneezing and coughing?
99240.e: Cold viruses are in the droplets from sneezing and coughing. That is how others catch it.

99241.q: Why do you keep your distance from people who are coughing a lot?
a: So you do not catch anything
99241.e: The droplets only fly a short distance. If you keep your distance, fewer germs reach you.
99241.m: Keeping your distance protects against infection.

99242.q: What do people in Switzerland often say when someone sneezes?
99242.e: When someone sneezes, you wish them “Gesundheit” (good health). “En Guete” is what you say before a meal.
99242.m: After a sneeze, you wish someone good health.

99243.q: Why is it better to stay at home with a fever and a cough?
a: So you do not infect others
99243.e: If you are ill, you recover faster at home. And you do not infect other children.
99243.m: If you are ill, you stay at home and protect others.

99244.q: What is a cotton bud good for, for example?
99244.e: You can use the cotton wool to paint dots of colour on paper. Cotton buds are also popular for crafts.
99244.m: You can paint dots with cotton buds.

99245.q: What is good for cleaning the outer ear when you wash?
99245.e: A damp flannel gently cleans the outer ear and behind the ear. Then you dry it well.
99245.m: You clean the outer ear with a flannel.

99246.q: Which part inside the ear can a cotton bud damage?
99246.e: The eardrum is a thin skin deep inside the ear. A cotton bud can damage it.

99247.q: Where on your ear may you use a cotton bud?
a: Only on the outside of the outer ear
99247.e: You can clean carefully on the outside of the outer ear. A cotton bud does not belong in the ear canal.
99247.m: Cotton buds are only for the outside of the ear.

99248.q: Where does a used cotton bud go?
99248.e: Cotton buds block pipes and sewage works. That is why they go in the bin.
99248.m: Cotton buds go in the bin.

99249.q: What is the tip of a cotton bud made of?
99249.e: Soft cotton wool is wrapped around the end of the stick. That is where the name comes from.
99249.m: A cotton bud has tips made of cotton wool.

99250.q: What do you do if your ear is blocked with earwax?
a: Wait a long time and say nothing
99250.e: A doctor can remove the earwax safely. Poking around in your ear yourself can hurt it.
99250.m: If your ears are blocked, the doctor can help.

99251.e: Earwax is usually yellow to brown. It is a soft, waxy substance.

99252.q: What do you wash your hair with?
99252.e: Shampoo is a liquid soap for your hair and scalp. It gets your hair clean.
99252.m: You wash your hair with shampoo.

99253.q: Do only children with unwashed hair get head lice?
a: No, it has nothing to do with dirt
99253.e: Lice climb from head to head, whether the hair is clean or not. It has nothing to do with dirt.

99254.q: Why do you close your eyes when you wash your hair?
99254.e: If shampoo gets in your eyes, it stings. With your eyes closed, that does not happen.
99254.m: Keep your eyes closed when washing your hair.

99255.q: What do you use to untangle wet hair?
99255.e: A wide-toothed comb loosens knots in your hair. You comb carefully from the bottom upwards.
99255.m: You untangle wet hair with a comb.

99256.q: What helps long hair to be combed more easily after washing?
99256.e: Conditioner makes hair soft and smooth. Then it gets fewer knots.

99257.q: Where do you massage the shampoo in well when you wash your hair?
a: On the back of your neck
99257.e: Grease and dandruff collect on the scalp. That is why you massage the shampoo in there with your fingertips.
99257.m: You massage shampoo into your scalp.

99258.q: Why should you never use a hairdryer next to a full bath?
a: You could get an electric shock
99258.e: If a hairdryer falls into the water, electricity can flow through the water. That can kill.
99258.m: Electricity and water are dangerous together.

99259.q: Why do you rinse the shampoo out well after washing?
a: So no traces stay on your scalp
99259.e: Leftover shampoo can irritate your scalp and make it itch. That is why you rinse until there is no more foam.

99260.q: How often should you change your socks?
99260.e: Your feet sweat into your socks all day. Fresh socks every day stop bad smells.
99260.m: You change your socks every day.

99261.e: Dirt, sweat and smells collect in clothes you have worn. Washing makes them clean again.

99262.q: What machine do people usually wash clothes with today?
99262.e: The washing machine washes clothes with water and washing powder. Then it spins the water out.
99262.m: Clothes are washed in the washing machine.

99263.q: What do you put on after PE?
99263.e: After sport, your PE kit is sweaty. Fresh clothes feel better and do not smell.
99263.m: After sport, you put on fresh clothes.

99264.q: What do the little pictures on a clothing label show?
99264.e: The care symbols show how warm you may wash it and whether you can iron it. That way the clothing does not get ruined.
99264.m: Care symbols tell you how to wash a piece of clothing.

99265.q: What does the number 30 in the washtub symbol on a label mean?
99265.e: The number in the washtub gives the highest washing temperature in degrees Celsius. If it is warmer, the clothing can shrink.
99265.m: The number in the washtub shows the highest washing temperature.

99266.q: Why do you not put wet clothes in the wardrobe?
99266.e: Mould grows easily in damp clothes, and they smell musty. That is why you let them dry first.
99266.m: Clothes only go into the wardrobe when dry.

99267.q: Where do you put dirty clothes?
99267.e: You collect dirty clothes in the laundry basket until they are washed. That way the clean clothes in the wardrobe stay clean.
99267.m: Dirty clothes belong in the laundry basket.

99268.q: Why do you keep your fingernails short?
99268.e: Dirt and germs get stuck under long nails. Short nails are easier to keep clean.

99269.q: What do you use to smooth rough edges on your fingernails?
99269.e: You rub the nail file gently over the edge of the nail. Then you no longer get caught on jumpers.
99269.m: A nail file smooths nail edges.

99270.q: What do you use to clean the dirt from under your fingernails?
99270.e: The small, hard nail brush gets well under the nails. With water and soap you scrub the dirt away.
99270.m: A nail brush gets your nails clean.

99271.q: Why should you not bite your fingernails?
99271.e: There are lots of germs on your fingers and under your nails. When you bite them, they go straight into your mouth.
99271.m: Nail biting puts germs in your mouth.

a: A small piece of skin sticking out at the edge of a nail
99272.e: A hangnail is a torn little piece of skin next to the nail. You cut it off carefully instead of pulling at it.
99272.m: A hangnail is a small tear in the skin by the nail.

99274.e: You collect clipped nails and throw them in the bin. That way they do not lie around.
99274.m: Clipped nails go in the bin.

99275.q: What is the right way to cut toenails?
99275.e: Toenails cut straight across do not grow into the skin so easily. Rounded corners can grow in.

99276.q: What can happen to a fingernail if you trap your finger hard?
99276.e: A bruise can form under the nail. Then the nail looks dark blue until it has grown out.
99276.m: A trapped finger can get a blue nail.

99277.q: What can you use to see bacteria?
99277.e: Bacteria are tiny and invisible to the naked eye. A microscope makes them look much bigger.
99277.m: You can only see bacteria with a microscope.

99278.q: Which food is made with the help of bacteria?
99278.e: Certain bacteria turn milk into yoghurt. The milk becomes thick and slightly sour.
99278.m: Yoghurt is made with the help of bacteria.

99279.q: Where in the body do lots of useful bacteria live?
99279.e: Countless bacteria live in the gut. They help to digest food.
99279.m: In the gut, bacteria help with digestion.

99280.q: Which medicine helps against illnesses caused by bacteria?
99280.e: Antibiotics kill bacteria or slow them down. But they do not help against viruses.

99281.e: Bacteria are living things made of just one single cell. They live almost everywhere on Earth.

99282.q: Where do bacteria especially like to multiply?
a: On hot stones in the sun
99282.e: Warmth and moisture make bacteria grow quickly. In the cold, they hardly multiply.
99282.m: Bacteria like it warm and damp.

99283.q: What can bacteria in your mouth cause if you do not brush your teeth?
99283.e: Bacteria in the mouth eat sugar and make acid. This acid attacks the teeth.
99283.m: Brushing your teeth protects against tooth decay.

99284.q: Where do used wet wipes go?
99284.e: Wet wipes do not break down in water and block the pipes. That is why you throw them in the bin.
99284.m: Wet wipes do not go down the toilet.

99285.q: What do you do after using the toilet?
99285.e: When you flush, everything goes away. Then the toilet is clean for the next person.
99285.m: Always flush after using the toilet.

99286.q: Why do you close the toilet lid before flushing?
a: So fewer splashes get into the air
99286.e: When you flush, tiny droplets splash up. A closed lid keeps them in.

99287.q: What do you often dry your hands with in a public toilet?
a: Paper towels or a hand dryer
99287.e: Public toilets have paper towels or a machine that blows warm air. That way your hands stay clean.
99287.m: In public toilets, you also dry your hands well.

99288.q: Why is it better not to take your mobile phone to the toilet?
99288.e: In the toilet, germs easily get onto your phone. Later you touch it again and hold it to your face.
99288.m: It is better to leave your phone outside when you go to the loo.

99289.q: What do you clean the toilet bowl with?
99289.e: The toilet brush stands next to the toilet. You use it to scrub dirt out of the bowl.
99289.m: The toilet brush cleans the toilet bowl.

99291.q: What do you do if the toilet roll is almost finished?
99291.e: That way the next person has enough paper too. If there is no roll, you tell an adult.
99291.m: If the paper is almost finished, you put out a new roll.

99292.q: Why do you slide down the slide by yourself?
99292.e: The Earth pulls all things towards it. This force is called gravity, and it makes you slide down the sloping slide.

99293.q: On which slide do you go faster?
a: On a very short gentle one
99293.e: The steeper the slide, the more strongly gravity pulls you along it. That is why you go faster.
99293.m: Steep slides are faster than gentle ones.

99294.q: What slows you down a little as you slide?
99294.e: When two surfaces rub against each other, it slows things down. This braking effect is called friction.

99295.q: What is the best way to brake on a slide?
99295.e: Rubber is grippy and rubs hard against the slide. That is why shoes with rubber soles brake well.
99295.m: Rubber brakes well because it is grippy.

99296.q: Why do you often slide faster on a wet slide?
99296.e: A thin film of water means you rub less against the slide. So you are slowed down less.
99296.m: Wet surfaces are often more slippery.

99297.q: Why can a metal slide be dangerous in summer?
99297.e: Metal gets very hot in strong sunshine. You can burn your skin on it, so test it with your hand first.
99297.m: Test metal in the sun with your hand first.

99298.q: Why does your hair sometimes stand on end after going down a plastic slide?
99298.e: Rubbing against plastic charges you up. Your hairs then have the same charge and push each other away.
99298.m: Rubbing against plastic can charge you up.

99299.q: Where does your speed on the slide come from?
a: From being high up at the top
From the noise of the children
From the colour of the slide
99299.e: When you climb up the ladder, you store energy by being high up. When you slide, it turns into movement.
99299.m: The higher you start, the more speed you get.

99300.q: What happens at the flat end of the slide?
a: You take off into the air
99300.e: At the flat end, gravity no longer pulls you forward. Friction slows you down until you stop.
99300.m: At the flat end the slide slows you down.

99301.q: What is an object that swings back and forth like a swing called?
99301.e: A pendulum is fixed at the top and swings back and forth. A swing is a big pendulum.

99302.q: How do you get going on a swing without being pushed?
a: Move your legs forwards and back
99302.e: If you stretch out your legs and pull them back in at the right moment, you give the swing a little energy with each swing.
99302.m: You can use your legs to get yourself going.

99303.q: Why does a swing go less and less high if nobody pushes it?
a: Air and friction slow it down
99303.e: The air and the friction at the top where it hangs slow the swing down a little. So it slowly gets smaller until it stops.
99303.m: Without a new push every swing stops.

99304.q: Where are you fastest on a swing?
a: Right at the bottom in the middle
Right at the top at the front
Right at the top at the back
99304.e: As you swing down you get faster and faster. Right at the bottom you have the greatest speed, after that you slow down again.
99304.m: A swing is fastest right at the bottom.

99305.q: Where does the swing stop for a very short moment?
99305.e: At the highest point the swing changes direction. There it stands still for a tiny moment.
99305.m: When it turns round, the swing stops briefly.

99306.q: When should you push a swing to make it go higher?
a: When it is moving away from you
When it is coming towards you
When it is hanging still and you pull
It does not matter when you push
99306.e: If you push in the same direction it is already swinging, it gets more speed. If you push against it, you slow it down.
99306.m: Always push a swing in the direction it is moving.

99307.q: Which swing swings back and forth faster?
a: The one with the biggest seat
99307.e: With a pendulum, it is mainly the length that decides how fast it swings back and forth. Short pendulums swing faster than long ones.
99307.m: Short pendulums swing faster than long ones.

99308.q: Does a heavy child on the same swing swing back and forth much more slowly than a light one?
99308.e: How fast a pendulum swings back and forth hardly depends on weight. What matters most is the length of the ropes.
99308.m: Weight hardly changes the rhythm of a swing.

99309.q: How does your body feel right at the top when the swing turns round?
99309.e: At the top, where it turns round, the seat hardly presses on you. That is why you feel very light for a moment and get butterflies in your tummy.
99309.m: At the top of a swing you feel light for a moment.

99310.q: In which direction are you pushed on a fast-spinning roundabout?
99310.e: Your body wants to keep flying straight on, but the roundabout steers you in a circle. That is why you feel a pull towards the edge.
99310.m: On a roundabout you are pulled towards the edge.

99311.q: Where on the roundabout are you moving fastest?
a: Halfway between the middle and the edge
99311.e: In one turn you travel a much bigger circle on the outside than on the inside. You have the same amount of time for it, so you are fastest on the outside.
99311.m: On the outside you spin fastest.

99312.q: Where on the spinning roundabout do you need to hold on least?
99312.e: In the middle you only turn around yourself and are hardly pulled outwards.
99312.m: The middle of the roundabout is the calmest place.

99313.q: Why do you feel dizzy after riding on a roundabout?
a: Your organ of balance is muddled
99313.e: In the inner ear there is an organ of balance with fluid in it. After spinning, the fluid keeps moving, so everything seems to spin.
99313.m: The organ of balance is in the ear.

99314.q: What does a roundabout need to start turning?
99314.e: Something that is standing still only moves when a force acts on it. On a playground roundabout, that is your push.

99315.q: What does a roundabout turn around?
a: The next piece of play equipment
99315.e: In the middle there is a fixed pole or bearing. The whole roundabout turns around it.
99315.m: A roundabout turns around its axle.

99316.q: What is the force you feel pulling you outwards on the roundabout called?
99316.e: Anyone moving in a circle feels a pull outwards. This is called centrifugal force.
99316.m: In a circle you feel centrifugal force.

99317.q: When is it safest to get off the roundabout?
a: When it is at its fastest
In the middle of a turn
99317.e: If you jump off a spinning roundabout, you take its speed with you and can fall. That is why you wait until it stops.
99317.m: Only get off when the roundabout has stopped.

99318.q: What does the mat of a trampoline do when you land on it?
99318.e: The mat gives way and is stretched downwards. Then it pulls back together and throws you up.
99318.m: A trampoline stores your energy and gives it back.

99319.q: What is attached around the edge of a trampoline between the mat and the frame?
99319.e: All the way round, many steel springs connect the mat to the frame. They stretch when you jump.
99319.m: Lots of springs hold the trampoline mat.

99320.q: Why does a garden trampoline often have a net all round it?
a: So that no rain falls in
99320.e: When jumping you can easily drift to the side. The net catches you before you fall onto the hard ground.

99321.q: How do you jump higher on a trampoline?
a: Bend your knees and push off hard
99321.e: If you bend your knees and push off hard, you press the mat down further. So it bounces you higher.
99321.m: Press the mat down further and you jump higher.

99322.q: Why is it dangerous if lots of children jump at the same time?
a: They can crash into each other
99322.e: Several jumpers disturb each other and easily bump together. That is why it is best to jump one at a time.
99322.m: On a trampoline it is best to jump alone.

99323.q: What do you call a material that goes back to its shape after being stretched?
99323.e: Elastic things such as rubber or a trampoline mat can be stretched. Afterwards they go back to their old shape.
99323.m: Elastic things spring back into shape.

99324.q: What covers the springs on a trampoline so that nobody gets hurt?
99324.e: There is a padded edge over the springs and the frame. If you land there, you do not get caught in the springs.
99324.m: The edge pad protects you from the springs.

99325.q: Where is it safest to jump on a trampoline?
99325.e: In the middle the mat bounces most evenly and you are far away from the hard frame.
99325.m: Jump in the middle of the trampoline.

99326.q: Why is it better to jump on a trampoline without shoes?
99326.e: Hard soles and little stones in the tread can wear the mat. Also, with shoes on you can hurt others more easily.
99326.m: Go on the trampoline without shoes.

99327.q: What is the place in the middle that the seesaw moves around called?
99327.e: The seesaw rests in the middle and tips around this place. It is called the pivot.
99327.m: A seesaw tips around its pivot.

99328.q: Why do many seesaws have a handle in front of the seat?
a: To hold on to when it bumps
99328.e: When the seesaw hits the bottom or reaches the top, there is a jolt. With the handle you hold on and do not fall off.
99328.m: Always hold the handle on a seesaw.

99329.q: Two children of the same weight sit equally far out. What happens?
a: One side hits the ground at once
99329.e: Both push down equally hard and equally far from the pivot. That is why the seesaw stays balanced.
99329.m: Equal weights at equal distances balance each other.

99330.q: How do you get back up on a seesaw?
99330.e: If you push off hard from the ground with your legs, your side rises. The other side then goes down.
99330.m: On a seesaw you push yourself up with your legs.

99331.q: Why is there often a piece of rubber or a car tyre under the ends of a seesaw?
a: So that the bump is soft
So that the seesaw goes faster
So that it looks more colourful
So that it does not get wet
99331.e: Without padding the seesaw would hit the ground hard. The rubber cushions the bump and protects your back.
99331.m: A rubber buffer makes the bump softer.

99332.q: What does the other side of the seesaw do when your side goes down?
99332.e: A seesaw is a straight beam with a pivot. If one end goes down, the other has to go up.
99332.m: On a seesaw one side always goes up and the other down.

99333.q: Why do you feel a jolt when your side of the seesaw hits the ground?
99333.e: You are moving down fast. When it hits the ground you are stopped very suddenly, and you feel that as a jolt.
99333.m: Stopping suddenly feels like a jolt.

99334.q: How can two small children lift an adult on a seesaw?
a: By sitting together right at the end
By sitting together in the middle
By sitting on the adult's side
By sitting apart on both sides
99334.e: Two children together are heavier than one. Right at the end of the long arm they also have the greatest leverage.
99334.m: Far out on a seesaw your weight has more effect.

99335.q: What happens if one child suddenly jumps off the seesaw while the other is up in the air?
a: The other one comes down hard
The other one flies even higher
The seesaw breaks in the middle
99335.e: Without a counterweight the seesaw tips straight down on the heavy side. The child at the top then hits the ground hard.
99335.m: Only get off once you have agreed it with each other.

99336.q: Why do you need a lot of strength in your arms when climbing?
99336.e: When you climb up, you lift your whole body. Your arms and legs work hard to do this.
99336.m: When climbing you lift your own weight.

99337.q: Why is there sand, gravel or bark chippings under a climbing frame?
a: So that a fall is softer
So that it is not dusty
99337.e: Soft ground gives way when someone falls. So you get hurt less than on tarmac.
99337.m: Soft ground protects you in a fall.

99338.q: At least how many hands and feet should be holding on when you climb?
99338.e: This is called the three-point rule: only one hand or foot moves, the other three hold on.
99338.m: When climbing, three points always hold on.

99339.q: Why are climbing frames often built from triangles?
99339.e: A triangle made of solid bars cannot be pushed out of shape without bending a bar. That makes frames especially stable.

99340.q: What should you take off before climbing in the playground?
99340.e: A bike helmet can get caught in bars or nets. Then the chin strap can become dangerous around your neck.
99340.m: Take off your bike helmet in the playground.

99341.q: Why should no cords hang down from your jacket when you climb?
99341.e: Loose cords and strings can get caught on bars or nets. That can be dangerous if you slip.
99341.m: Put loose strings away when climbing.

99342.q: What is the best way to land when you jump down from the frame?
99342.e: If you bend your knees when you land, your impact is slowed down more gently. That protects your joints and bones.
99342.m: Bend your knees when you land.

99343.q: Why does a big climbing frame not tip over when lots of children climb on it?
a: It is firmly anchored in the ground
It is tied to a tree with ropes
It is filled with air inside
99343.e: The posts go deep into the ground, often into concrete. That way the frame cannot tip over.
99343.m: Solid foundations keep play equipment safe.

99344.q: What does the seat of a zip line hang from on the cable?
99344.e: At the top of the seat there is a trolley with pulleys. The pulleys run along the tight cable.
99344.m: On a zip line a trolley rolls along the cable.

99345.q: Why do you start moving on the zip line by yourself?
a: The start is higher than the finish
The wind always blows that way
99345.e: The cable is fixed higher at the start than at the end. So gravity makes you roll down.
99345.m: A zip line slopes down from start to finish.
